story.title: China Vows to Safeguard Interests Amid US Sanctions on Iran
story.summary: China has condemned the US for threatening sanctions against nations that continue to engage in trade with Iran. Beijing stated it would take 'all necessary measures' to protect its interests, particularly in light of its significant oil imports from Tehran. The Chinese government characterized the US sanctions as illegal and expressed its commitment to maintaining its trade relations with Iran.

timeline_highlights.title: US Prepares Major Sanctions Against Iran Amidst Threats of Retaliation
timeline_highlights.summary: The US is set to announce new economic sanctions against Iran, described by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent as the 'greatest financial offensive ever marshaled.' This initiative, termed 'economic D-Day' by the Trump administration, aims to isolate Iran economically and target its trade partners. In response, Iran has threatened to retaliate against any nation that supports these sanctions, calling such actions an 'act of war.'

timeline_highlights.title: US Treasury Secretary Initiates 'Operation Economic Outcast' to Target Iran
timeline_highlights.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced 'Operation Economic Outcast' aimed at isolating Iran economically. He stated that any entity facilitating money laundering for Iran would be excluded from the US dollar system. Concurrently, the Iranian rial fell to a record low of approximately 2.02 million to the dollar, as Bessent warned of an impending 'economic D-Day' for Iran.

event_overview.title: About Iran Sanctions
event_overview.subject: Iran Sanctions
event_overview.summary: Iran sanctions are a set of U.S. and international restrictive measures directed at Iranian government bodies, companies, individuals, and specified economic activity. In the United States, the measures combine statutes, presidential executive orders, and Treasury regulations; they are used in connection with concerns including nuclear proliferation, terrorism, missile activity, human-rights abuses, and sanctions evasion, while some humanitarian trade remains authorized or licensable.

facts.label: U.S. administration and legal framework
facts.value: The U.S. Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) administers the Iran sanctions program. OFAC says it implements multiple legal authorities, including executive orders, congressional statutes, regulations in 31 CFR Parts 535, 560, 561 and 562, and—in relevant cases—UN Security Council resolutions.

facts.label: Core U.S. trade restrictions
facts.value: The Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, 31 CFR Part 560, contain prohibitions affecting imports, exports or reexports, trade-related dealings, investment, facilitation by U.S. persons, and transactions involving blocked property, subject to stated exceptions and licenses.

facts.label: Historical baseline
facts.value: A U.S. import embargo on Iranian-origin goods and services was imposed by Executive Order 12613 on October 29, 1987; comprehensive U.S. trade and financial sanctions followed in 1995 under Executive Order 12959. The present framework has subsequently been expanded and amended through further statutory and executive authorities.

facts.label: Humanitarian channels
facts.value: Sanctions do not amount to a blanket ban on humanitarian goods: OFAC maintains authorizations and licensing processes for agricultural commodities, medicine and medical devices, though restrictions can still apply where transactions involve designated parties or other prohibited activity.

facts.label: UN nuclear-related measures
facts.value: At the UN level, Security Council resolution 2231 of July 20, 2015 endorsed the JCPOA and replaced earlier Iran nuclear-related measures. The Security Council states that, effective September 27, 2025, the earlier resolutions’ provisions were reapplied through the resolution 2231 process and the 1737 sanctions list was re-established.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the August 23–24, 2026 U.S.-Iran sanctions-threat escalation and stated retaliation risks; it does not attempt to catalog the full history of every designation, legal authority, exemption, or diplomatic dispute.

related_stories.title: Trump Administration Plans to Revoke Visas of Up to 200,000 Asylum Seekers
related_stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing to revoke the visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum in the United States. This action could represent the largest mass visa revocation in U.S. history, targeting individuals who entered the country on tourist or business visas.
